skill.name: generating-product-photos
skill.description: Creates commercial product photography prompts and generated images from a product reference, supporting studio, lifestyle, hero, on-model, close-up, flat-lay, seasonal, infographic, creative, and floating formats.
skill.summary: Directs consistent commercial product images across ten photography modes.
skill.author: supercmohq

security_audit.summary: All 48 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and ordinary photography prose. One high-severity semantic finding remains: the skill instructs agents to reframe and switch models after safety or policy rejection.

remediation.issue: The failure workflow retries safety or policy rejections with a stand-in and another image model.
remediation.suggestion: Stop after a safety or policy rejection. Explain the limitation and request a clearly compliant alternative without switching providers to bypass the decision.

semantic_findings.description: After a safety or policy rejection, the skill directs the agent to use a stand-in, resubmit, and then switch models. This can circumvent a provider safety decision instead of stopping or seeking compliant clarification.

content.value_statement: Creating consistent product imagery requires careful control of identity, lighting, composition, and output format. This skill analyzes a reference and directs generation across ten commercial photography modes.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes a supplied product image before composing generation prompts.
Routes requests across ten formats, including studio, lifestyle, hero, flat-lay, infographic, and on-model photography.
Preserves product shape, color, label, texture, design, and physical state through reference-image instructions.
Specifies lighting, shadows, optics, materials, composition, and color using commercial photography language.
Builds coordinated multi-image sets with consistent references, models, palettes, lighting, and camera choices.
Selects image models and request settings based on text, layout, fallback, crop, and resolution needs.
limitations: A source photo is required for reliable product identity and packaging fidelity.
Generated labels, hands, faces, reflections, and fine geometry may still contain image-model errors.
Each generated frame can incur provider charges, and automatic quality regeneration is intentionally limited.
Marketplace listing galleries and images without a product subject are outside the supported scope.

use_cases.title: Build Ecommerce Packshots
use_cases.description: Create consistent studio views with accurate color, controlled backgrounds, sharp detail, and grounded shadows for product pages.

use_cases.title: Develop Campaign Visuals
use_cases.description: Plan hero, lifestyle, seasonal, and creative frames around a shared product reference and brand direction.

use_cases.title: Produce Client Concepts
use_cases.description: Translate a creative brief into production-ready photography prompts with defined lighting, optics, staging, and crops.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Studio Packshot
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one clean product image
prompt_templates.prompt: Create one clean studio packshot from the attached product photo. Use a neutral seamless background, accurate color, full-product sharpness, and one natural contact shadow.

prompt_templates.title: Stage a Lifestyle Scene
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with audience and placement context
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a lifestyle image for [target buyer] using the attached product. Place it in [setting] at [time], with believable use and a [aspect ratio] crop.

prompt_templates.title: Direct an On-Model Image
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed request involving casting and product interaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an on-model image for [channel]. Show [casting details] using the attached product through its real physical action, with [wardrobe], [crop], and [lighting].

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Coordinated Campaign Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan [number] campaign frames for [placements] using one attached product reference. Define each frame, then maintain one palette, lighting setup, model, and camera language throughout.

output_examples.input: Generate a clean studio image of this skincare bottle for a square product page.
output_examples.output: A square three-quarter packshot with a seamless pale-gray sweep, neutral daylight color, full-bottle sharpness, and a soft contact shadow.

output_examples.input: Create three coordinated summer campaign images for this insulated bottle.
output: Hero frame: the bottle stands against a bright coastal palette with controlled side light and clear copy space.
Lifestyle frame: the same bottle appears beside a beach towel and book under matching daylight.
Detail frame: a close crop shows the lid material and condensation with the same palette and light direction.

output_examples.input: Make a vertical social advertisement with two supplied feature callouts.
output_examples.output: A vertical infographic image that preserves the reference product, places the exact callouts with clear hierarchy, and uses anchored leader lines.

best_practices: Supply a clear, high-resolution product image and state any required product position or moving-part state.
Name the destination, aspect ratio, buyer, brand constraints, and number of frames before generation.
Approve a frame list before generating a set because every frame may create a separate provider charge.
anti_patterns: Do not describe label text from memory because the image model may redraw it incorrectly.
Do not mix unrelated settings, lighting styles, or image models within one coordinated set.
Do not request extra comparison images or retries without explicit approval for additional generation charges.

faq.question: Do I need a product photo?
faq.answer: A photo is strongly recommended. Without one, the skill relies on written details and cannot reliably preserve packaging identity.

faq.question: Which photography formats are supported?
faq.answer: It supports studio, lifestyle, hero, on-model, close-up, flat-lay, seasonal, infographic, creative, and floating product images.

faq.question: Can it create several images at once?
faq.answer: Yes. It first defines the frame list, then keeps references, model choice, palette, lighting, and camera language consistent.

faq.question: Can it add text and feature callouts?
faq.answer: Yes. Infographic mode handles exact supplied wording, visual hierarchy, anchor points, leader lines, and placement.

faq.question: How does it preserve the original product?
faq.answer: It attaches the same reference image and repeats explicit fidelity instructions for shape, color, label, texture, design, and state.

faq.question: Will it automatically fix a weak result?
faq.answer: No. It returns the result for review and avoids unapproved regeneration because each additional image may create another charge.
